title: Choose where the EMR runtime should live
description: Select a workload shape and the platform constraint that matters most. The lab exposes which EMR deployment option directly satisfies each requirement.
modelNote: Capability matching is a decision aid, not a benchmark. EMR release support, Region availability, quotas, networking, IAM, startup behavior, and price must be validated against the current AWS documentation and a representative workload.

capabilities.automatic-capacity: capacity acquired and released without operating a cluster
capabilities.kubernetes-platform: reuse an existing Amazon EKS control plane and tenancy model
capabilities.broad-frameworks: cluster software beyond Spark, including Hadoop ecosystem services
capabilities.host-control: direct control of EC2 topology, bootstrap actions, and local storage
capabilities.long-lived-services: persistent cluster services and cluster-local HDFS

scenarios.label: Bursty Spark batch
scenarios.detail: Scheduled Spark jobs arrive unevenly and should release workers when complete.

scenarios.label: Shared Kubernetes analytics
scenarios.detail: A platform team already operates EKS and wants Spark jobs inside that tenancy boundary.

scenarios.label: Persistent Hadoop ecosystem
scenarios.detail: The workload needs long-lived services, cluster-local storage, or broad host-level configuration.

priorities.label: Minimize cluster operations
priorities.detail: Do not own worker provisioning, idle capacity, or node replacement.

priorities.label: Reuse the EKS platform
priorities.detail: Keep compute governance and tenancy aligned with existing Kubernetes operations.

priorities.label: Control hosts and storage
priorities.detail: Choose EC2 topology, local disks, bootstrap actions, and cluster services directly.

options.label: EMR Serverless
options.operatorOwns: Applications, release selection, job configuration, IAM runtime roles, data, and limits.
options.runtimeScope: Serverless Spark and Hive applications with workers managed by the service.
constraints: No EC2 cluster topology or cluster-local HDFS to manage
Framework scope is narrower than EMR on EC2

options.label: EMR on EKS
options.operatorOwns: The EKS cluster, namespaces, compute capacity, networking, access, and Kubernetes operations.
options.runtimeScope: EMR-managed Apache Spark jobs submitted through virtual clusters on Amazon EKS.
constraints: Does not provide the broad persistent Hadoop cluster model

options.label: EMR on EC2
options.operatorOwns: Cluster lifecycle, instance fleets or groups, storage topology, release configuration, and scaling bounds.
options.runtimeScope: The broadest EMR cluster application catalog, including Spark and Hadoop ecosystem services.
constraints: The team owns cluster capacity and lifecycle choices
Idle and failed capacity need explicit controls
